failure_summary.description: Agents chose related compounds, yes/no responses, or salient nearby entities despite existing guidance to identify the requested slot and verify the full clue.
Answers used a noncanonical expanded or abbreviated name instead of the expected entity label.
A bare title-and-year prompt led to a generic category answer because no rule covers inferring a title's relevant person from its context.

patch.reasoning: Most failures already violate existing clue-slot, evidence-check, or granularity rules, so repeating them would not patch a skill gap. Add guidance only for title-and-year prompts that provide no explicit relation.

edits.content:
## Bare work-title prompts
- If a prompt consists only of a work title and year, do not answer with its generic type (such as “film”). Look for a principal person explicitly and centrally associated with that work in the context, such as its director, author, or creator, and answer with that person only when the association is clear. If the context offers no clear intended relation, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.
